sanskrit: prāptarājyasya rāmasya vālmīkir bhagavān ṛṣiḥ cakāra caritaṃ kṛtsnaṃ vicitrapadam ātmavān
english: The venerable sage Vālmīki, self-possessed, composed the entire life-story of Rāma who had attained his kingdom — a narrative adorned with wondrous words.

sanskrit: kṛtvā tu tan mahāprājñaḥ sabhaviṣyaṃ sahottaram cintayām āsa ko nv etat prayuñjīyād iti prabhuḥ
english: Having composed that work — complete with what was yet to come and with the Uttara-kāṇḍa — the greatly wise master then pondered: who indeed could perform this?

sanskrit: tasya cintayamānasya maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ agṛhṇītāṃ tataḥ pādau muniveṣau kuśīlavau
english: While the great seer of purified soul was thus reflecting, two wandering bards clad in the garb of ascetics — Kuśa and Lava — then clasped his feet.

sanskrit: kuśīlavau tu dharmajñau rājaputrau yaśasvinau bhrātarau svarasaṃpannau dadarśāśramavāsinau
english: He saw that those two — Kuśa and Lava — were royal princes endowed with righteousness, illustrious brothers blessed with melodious voices, dwelling in his hermitage.

sanskrit: sa tu medhāvinau dṛṣṭvā vedeṣu pariniṣṭhitau vedopabṛhmaṇārthāya tāv agrāhayata prabhuḥ
english: Seeing them to be gifted with keen intellect and thoroughly grounded in the Vedas, the master caused them to learn this poem as a supplement and amplification of the Vedas.

sanskrit: kāvyaṃ rāmāyaṇaṃ kṛtsnaṃ sītāyāś caritaṃ mahat paulastya vadham ity eva cakāra caritavrataḥ
english: The one steadfast in his vow composed the entire poem — the Rāmāyaṇa — the great story of Sītā, known also as the slaying of Paulastya (Rāvaṇa).

sanskrit: pāṭhye geye ca madhuraṃ pramāṇais tribhir anvitam jātibhiḥ saptabhir baddhaṃ tantrīlayasamanvitam
english: Sweet whether recited or sung, composed in the three metres, bound in the seven classes of musical notes, and harmonised with the rhythm of the lute —

sanskrit: hāsyaśṛṅgārakāruṇyaraudravīrabhayānakaiḥ bībhatsādirasair yuktaṃ kāvyam etad agāyatām
english: — this poem, infused with the rasas of the comic, the erotic, the pathetic, the furious, the heroic, the terrible, and the repulsive and the rest, the two of them sang.

sanskrit: tau tu gāndharvatattvajñau mūrcchanāsthānakovidau bhrātarau svarasaṃpannau gandharvāv iva rūpiṇau
english: Those two brothers, skilled in the science of the Gandharva art of music, expert in the modulations and the proper placements of notes, endowed with melodious voices, resembled Gandharvas in their form.

sanskrit: rūpalakṣaṇasaṃpannau madhurasvarabhāṣiṇau bimbād ivoddhṛtau bimbau rāmadehāt tathāparau
english: Endowed with the marks of auspicious beauty, speaking with sweet voices, they seemed like two images drawn forth from a single original — as if lifted from the very body of Rāma himself.

sanskrit: tau rājaputrau kārtsnyena dharmyam ākhyānam uttamam vāco vidheyaṃ tat sarvaṃ kṛtvā kāvyam aninditau
english: Those two blameless princes, having made the entire poem wholly subject to speech — reciting the righteous and excellent narrative in full — sang it.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇāṃ ca dvijātīnāṃ sādhūnāṃ ca samāgame yathopadeśaṃ tattvajñau jagatus tau samāhitau mahātmānau mahābhāgau sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitau
english: In assemblies of sages, twice-born ones, and holy men, those two great souls — supremely fortunate, adorned with every auspicious mark, knowers of truth — composed of mind, sang it in accordance with the teaching they had received.

sanskrit: tau kadā cit sametānām ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām āsīnānāṃ samīpasthāv idaṃ kāvyam agāyatām
english: On one occasion, standing near an assembly of purified-souled sages who had gathered and were seated together, those two sang this poem.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā munayaḥ sarve bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇāḥ sādhu sādhv ity tāv ūcatuḥ paraṃ vismayam āgatāḥ
english: Hearing it, all the sages — their eyes brimming with tears — said to those two, 'Well done! Well done!' and were filled with the utmost wonder.

sanskrit: te prītamanasaḥ sarve munayo dharmavatsalāḥ praśaśaṃsuḥ praśastavyau gāyamānau kuśīlavau
english: All those sages, joyful at heart and devoted to righteousness, praised Kuśa and Lava, those two who were indeed worthy of praise, as they sang.

sanskrit: aho gītasya mādhuryaṃ ślokānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ ciranirvṛttam apy etat pratyakṣam iva darśitam
english: "Ah, what sweetness in the singing — and especially in the verses! Even these events long past are displayed as if directly before our eyes."

sanskrit: praviśya tāv ubhau suṣṭhu tadā bhāvam agāyatām sahitau madhuraṃ raktaṃ saṃpannaṃ svarasaṃpadā
english: Those two, having entered fully and well into the feeling of the narrative, sang it together — melodiously, with deep emotion, rich with the wealth of their voices.

sanskrit: evaṃ praśasyamānau tau tapaḥślāghyair maharṣibhiḥ saṃraktataram atyarthaṃ madhuraṃ tāv agāyatām
english: Thus praised by the great seers praiseworthy for their austerities, those two sang with even greater passion and with surpassing sweetness.

sanskrit: prītaḥ kaś cin munis tābhyāṃ saṃsthitaḥ kalaśaṃ dadau prasanno valkalaṃ kaś cid dadau tābhyāṃ mahāyaśāḥ
english: One sage, delighted, gave them a water-pot; another of great fame, greatly pleased, gave them bark garments.

sanskrit: āścaryam idam ākhyānaṃ muninā saṃprakīrtitam paraṃ kavīnām ādhāraṃ samāptaṃ ca yathākramam
english: "This narrative, proclaimed by the sage, is a wonder — the supreme foundation for all poets — and it is brought to completion in due order."

sanskrit: praśasyamānau sarvatra kadā cit tatra gāyakau rathyāsu rājamārgeṣu dadarśa bharatāgrajaḥ
english: On one occasion, the elder brother of Bharata — Rāma — saw those two singers, who were praised everywhere, in the streets and on the royal highway.

sanskrit: svaveśma cānīya tato bhrātarau sakuśīlavau pūjayām āsa pūjārhau rāmaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
english: Rāma, the subduer of enemies, then brought those two brothers — Kuśa and Lava together — to his own palace and honoured them, who were worthy of honour.

sanskrit: āsīnaḥ kāñcane divye sa ca siṃhāsane prabhuḥ upopaviṣṭaiḥ sacivair bhrātṛbhiś ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: That lord, the scorcher of foes, was seated on a divine golden throne, with his ministers and brothers seated around him.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu rūpasaṃpannau tāv ubhau vīṇinau tataḥ uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmaḥ śatrughnaṃ bharataṃ tathā
english: Seeing those two endowed with beauty, carrying lutes, Rāma then spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, Śatrughna, and Bharata:

sanskrit: śrūyatām idam ākhyānaṃ anayor devavarcasoḥ vicitrārthapadaṃ samyag gāyator madhurasvaram
english: "Let this narrative be heard — sung properly by these two who shine with divine radiance, a narrative of wondrous meaning and verse, with sweet voices."

sanskrit: imau munī pārthivalakṣmaṇānvitau kuśīlavau caiva mahātapasvinau mamāpi tad bhūtikaraṃ pracakṣate mahānubhāvaṃ caritaṃ nibodhata
english: "These two ascetics — endowed with royal marks, Kuśa and Lava — are mighty in austerities. They recite a narrative of great power and glory that brings prosperity even to me. Listen to it."

sanskrit: tatas tu tau rāmavacaḥ pracoditāv agāyatāṃ mārgavidhānasaṃpadā sa cāpi rāmaḥ pariṣadgataḥ śanair bubhūṣayāsaktamanā babhūva ha
english: Then those two, urged on by Rāma's word, sang with the perfection of the proper method and manner; and Rāma himself, seated in the assembly, gradually became absorbed in mind, eager to hear more.

sanskrit: sarvāpūrvam iyaṃ yeṣām āsīt kṛtsnā vasuṃdharā prajāpatim upādāya nṛpāṇāṃ jayaśālinām
english: This entire earth was formerly theirs alone — those victorious kings, beginning with Prajāpati himself.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ sa sagaro nāma sāgaro yena khānitaḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇi yaṃ yāntaṃ paryavārayan
english: Among them was Sagara by name — he by whom the ocean was excavated, whose sixty thousand sons encircled him as he journeyed.

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇām idaṃ teṣāṃ rājñāṃ vaṃśe mahātmanām mahad utpannam ākhyānaṃ rāmāyaṇam iti śrutam
english: In the lineage of those kings of the Ikṣvāku dynasty, great souls, a great narrative was born — known as the Rāmāyaṇa.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ vartayiṣyāmi sarvaṃ nikhilam āditaḥ dharmakāmārthasahitaṃ śrotavyam anasūyayā
english: This I shall narrate in full, entirely from the beginning — replete with righteousness, love, and worldly purpose — and it is to be heard without envy.

sanskrit: kosalo nāma muditaḥ sphīto janapado mahān niviṣṭaḥ sarayūtīre prabhūtadhanadhānyavān
english: There is a great and prosperous country called Kosala, joyful and abundant, settled on the bank of the Sarayū river, rich in wealth and grain.

sanskrit: ayodhyā nāma nagarī tatrāsīl lokaviśrutā manunā mānavendreṇa yā purī nirmitā svayam
english: There stood a city famous throughout the world, called Ayodhyā — a city that Manu himself, the lord of men, had personally founded.

sanskrit: āyatā daśa ca dve ca yojanāni mahāpurī śrīmatī trīṇi vistīrṇā suvibhaktamahāpathā
english: That great and splendid city extended twelve yojanas in length and three in breadth, with its great avenues well laid out.

sanskrit: rājamārgeṇa mahatā suvibhaktena śobhitā muktapuṣpāvakīrṇena jalasiktena nityaśaḥ
english: It was adorned with a great royal road, well planned, strewn always with scattered flowers and sprinkled with water.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu rājā daśaratho mahārāṣṭravivardhanaḥ purīm āvāsayām āsa divi devapatir yathā
english: King Daśaratha, who expanded a great realm, caused that city to be inhabited, even as the lord of the gods dwells in heaven.

sanskrit: kapāṭatoraṇavatīṃ suvibhaktāntarāpaṇām sarvayantrāyudhavatīm upetāṃ sarvaśilpibhiḥ
english: It had gates and triumphal arches, its market streets were well arranged within, it was stocked with every kind of war-engine and weapon, and it was filled with artisans of every craft.

sanskrit: sūtamāgadhasaṃbādhāṃ śrīmatīm atulaprabhām uccāṭṭāladhvajavatīṃ śataghnīśatasaṃkulām
english: It was thronged with bards and panegyrists, splendid, of incomparable brilliance, furnished with lofty watchtowers and flags, and crowded with hundreds of śataghnī engines of war.

sanskrit: vadhūnāṭakasaṅghaiś ca saṃyuktāṃ sarvataḥ purīm udyānāmravaṇopetāṃ mahatīṃ sālamekhalām
english: The great city everywhere was filled with troops of female dancers and theatrical companies; it was provided with pleasure gardens and mango groves, and encircled by a girdle of śāla trees.

sanskrit: durgagambhīraparikhāṃ durgām anyair durāsadām vājivāraṇasaṃpūrṇāṃ gobhir uṣṭraiḥ kharais tathā
english: It had a deep and formidable moat making it a fortress difficult for others to assail; and it was filled with horses and elephants, and with cows, camels, and donkeys as well.

sanskrit: sāmantarājasaṅghaiś ca balikarmabhir āvṛtām nānādeśanivāsaiś ca vaṇigbhir upaśobhitām
english: It was surrounded by assemblies of subordinate kings engaged in rendering tribute, and it was adorned with merchants dwelling there from many different lands.

sanskrit: prasādai ratnavikṛtaiḥ parvatair upaśobhitām kūṭāgāraiś ca saṃpūrṇām indrasyevāmarāvatīm
english: Adorned with palaces fashioned of jewels that rose like mountains, filled with pinnacled mansions — it resembled Indra's Amarāvatī.

sanskrit: citrām aṣṭāpadākārāṃ varanārīgaṇair yutām sarvaratnasamākīrṇāṃ vimānagṛhaśobhitām
english: Variegated and laid out in the form of a chessboard, filled with crowds of noble women, strewn with gems of every kind, and beautified with mansioned houses —

sanskrit: gṛhagāḍhām avicchidrāṃ samabhūmau niveśitām śālitaṇḍulasaṃpūrṇām ikṣukāṇḍarasodakām
english: — densely packed with dwellings without gap, built on level ground, filled with śāli rice, and with water sweet as the juice of sugar-cane.

sanskrit: dundubhībhir mṛdaṅgaiś ca vīṇābhiḥ paṇavais tathā nāditāṃ bhṛśam atyarthaṃ pṛthivyāṃ tām anuttamām
english: Resounding exceedingly — and beyond all measure — with kettledrums, mṛdaṅgas, lutes, and paṇava drums, that peerless city on earth —

sanskrit: vimānam iva siddhānāṃ tapasādhigataṃ divi suniveśitaveśmāntāṃ narottamasamāvṛtām
english: — like the aerial palace of the Siddhas attained in heaven through austerities, its inner quarters of dwellings perfectly arranged, filled with the best of men.

sanskrit: ye ca bāṇair na vidhyanti viviktam aparāparam śabdavedhyaṃ ca vitataṃ laghuhastā viśāradāḥ
english: Those who would not miss shooting — clearly, at moving targets, one after another, and at distant ones perceivable only by sound — light of hand and expert:

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghravarāhāṇāṃ mattānāṃ nadatāṃ vane hantāro niśitaiḥ śastrair balād bāhubalair api
english: — slayers with sharp weapons of roaring, frenzied lions, tigers, and boars in the forest, and also by sheer strength of arm —

sanskrit: tādṛśānāṃ sahasrais tām abhipūrṇāṃ mahārathaiḥ purīm āvāsayām āsa rājā daśarathas tadā
english: — with thousands of such great warriors, King Daśaratha at that time caused that city to be garrisoned and inhabited.

sanskrit: tām agnimadbhir guṇavadbhir āvṛtāṃ dvijottamair vedaṣaḍaṅgapāragaiḥ sahasradaiḥ satyaratair mahātmabhir maharṣikalpair ṛṣibhiś ca kevalaiḥ
english: That city was surrounded by the foremost of the twice-born — maintainers of the sacred fire, men of virtuous excellence, masters of the six auxiliary sciences of the Veda, givers of thousands in gifts, devoted to truth, great souls equal to great seers, and by seers who were pure ascetics alone.

sanskrit: puryāṃ tasyām ayodhyāyāṃ vedavit sarvasaṃgrahaḥ dīrghadarśī mahātejāḥ paurajānapadapriyaḥ
english: In that city of Ayodhyā dwelt one who was a knower of the Vedas, all-encompassing in counsel, far-sighted, of great splendour, beloved of the city-folk and the country-people —

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇām atiratho yajvā dharmarato vaśī maharṣikalpo rājarṣis triṣu lokṛṣu viśrutaḥ
english: — the foremost chariot-warrior among the Ikṣvākus, a performer of sacrifices, devoted to righteousness, self-controlled, equal to a great sage, a royal seer renowned in all three worlds.

sanskrit: balavān nihatāmitro mitravān vijitendriyaḥ dhanaiś ca saṃcayaiś cānyaiḥ śakravaiśravaṇopamaḥ
english: Mighty, his enemies slain, rich in allies, his senses mastered, in his accumulations of wealth and other treasures comparable to Śakra and Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera).

sanskrit: yathā manur mahātejā lokasya parirakṣitā tathā daśaratho rājā vasañ jagad apālayat
english: Just as the great and resplendent Manu was the protector of all beings, so King Daśaratha, dwelling there, protected the entire world.

sanskrit: tena satyābhisaṃdhena trivargam anutiṣṭhatā pālitā sā purī śreṣṭhendreṇa ivāmarāvatī
english: By him — true to his pledged word, practising the three ends of life — that city was protected, as Amarāvatī is by the foremost of Indras.

sanskrit: tasmin puravare hṛṣṭā dharmātmanā bahuśrutāḥ narās tuṣṭādhanaiḥ svaiḥ svair alubdhāḥ satyavādinaḥ
english: In that best of cities, under that righteous-souled king, the men were cheerful, deeply learned, content with their own respective possessions, free from greed, and speakers of truth.

sanskrit: nālpasaṃnicayaḥ kaś cid āsīt tasmin purottame kuṭumbī yo hy asiddhārtho 'gavāśvadhanadhānyavān
english: There was no householder in that best of cities who had small savings — none who lacked fulfilment of his aims, and none without cattle, horses, wealth, and grain.

sanskrit: kāmī vā na kadaryo vā nṛśaṃsaḥ puruṣaḥ kva cit draṣṭuṃ śakyam ayodhyāyāṃ nāvidvān na ca nāstikaḥ
english: In Ayodhyā could nowhere be found a man who was lustful, or a miser, or cruel; nor one who was unlearned, nor one who denied the existence of the gods.

sanskrit: sarve narāś ca nāryaś ca dharmaśīlāḥ susaṃyatāḥ muditāḥ śīlavṛttābhyāṃ maharṣaya ivāmalāḥ
english: All men and women were righteous in conduct, well restrained, joyful, pure in character and deportment — like spotless great seers.

sanskrit: nākuṇḍalī nāmukuṭī nāsragvī nālpabhogavān nāmṛṣṭo nānuliptāṅgo nāsugandhaś ca vidyate
english: None was to be found without ear-ornaments, none without a diadem, none without a garland, none of scanty enjoyments; none was without clean garments, none without anointed limbs, none without fragrant scents.

sanskrit: nāmṛṣṭabhojī nādātā nāpy anaṅgadaniṣkadhṛk nāhastābharaṇo vāpi dṛśyate nāpy anātmavān
english: None was seen who ate without washing, none who was not a giver, none without upper-arm bands and golden neck-ornaments, none without hand-ornaments, none who lacked self-possession.

sanskrit: nānāhitāgnir nāyajvā vipro nāpy asahasradaḥ kaś cid āsīd ayodhyāyāṃ na ca nirvṛttasaṃkaraḥ
english: In Ayodhyā there was no brāhmaṇa who had not established the sacred fires, none who had not performed sacrifice, none who had not given thousands in gifts — and none who had allowed inter-caste confusion.

sanskrit: svakarmaniratā nityaṃ brāhmaṇā vijitendriyāḥ dānādhyayanaśīlāś ca saṃyatāś ca pratigrahe
english: The brāhmaṇas were always engaged in their proper duties, their senses mastered, devoted to giving and to study, and restrained in receiving gifts.

sanskrit: na nāstiko nānṛtako na kaś cid abahuśrutaḥ nāsūyako na cāśakto nāvidvān vidyate tadā
english: At that time there was found none who denied the gods, none who spoke falsehood, none who was not widely learned, none who was envious, none who was incapable, none who was unlearned.

sanskrit: na dīnaḥ kṣiptacitto vā vyathito vāpi kaś cana kaś cin naro vā nārī vā nāśrīmān nāpy arūpavān draṣṭuṃ śakyam ayodhyāyāṃ nāpi rājanyabhaktimān
english: None who was wretched or of distracted mind, or afflicted with suffering; in Ayodhyā no man nor woman was to be seen who lacked prosperity or who was of ill form, nor any who lacked devotion to the kṣatriya sovereign.

sanskrit: varṇeṣv agryacaturtheṣu devatātithipūjakāḥ dīrghāyuṣo narāḥ sarve dharmaṃ satyaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ
english: In the four varṇas foremost among them, all the men were worshippers of gods and guests, long-lived, devoted to righteousness and truth.

sanskrit: kṣatraṃ brahmamukhaṃ cāsīd vaiśyāḥ kṣatram anuvratāḥ śūdrāḥ svadharmaniratās trīn varṇān upacāriṇaḥ
english: The kṣatriyas were guided by the brāhmaṇas; the vaiśyas were devoted in their vows to the kṣatriyas; and the śūdras, engaged in their own prescribed duty, were in service to the three varṇas.

sanskrit: sā tenekṣvākunāthena purī suparirakṣitā yathā purastān manunā mānavendreṇa dhīmatā
english: That city was well protected by that lord of the Ikṣvāku line, even as it had been in former times by the wise Manu, the lord of men.

sanskrit: yodhānām agnikalpānāṃ peśalānām amarṣiṇām saṃpūrṇākṛtavidyānāṃ guhākesariṇām iva
english: It was full of warriors equal to fire — skilled, intolerant of insult, their martial education fully mastered, like lions in their mountain caves —

sanskrit: kāmbojaviṣaye jātair bāhlīkaiś ca hayottamaiḥ vanāyujair nadījaiś ca pūrṇāharihayopamaiḥ
english: — filled with the finest horses born in the Kāmboja country and among the Bāhlīkas, those trained in the forests and those born beside rivers, resembling Hari's own horses —

sanskrit: vindhyaparvatajair mattaiḥ pūrṇā haimavatair api madānvitair atibalair mātaṅgaiḥ parvatopamaiḥ
english: — filled with maddened elephants born of the Vindhya mountains and from the Himavat ranges — mighty elephants drunk with ichor, of surpassing strength, resembling mountains —

sanskrit: añjanād api niṣkrāntair vāmanād api ca dvipaiḥ bhadramandrair bhadramṛgair mṛgamandraiś ca sā purī
english: — that city was filled with elephants descended from Añjana and from Vāmana as well: of the bhadramandra, bhadramṛga, and mṛgamandra kinds.

sanskrit: nityamattaiḥ sadā pūrṇā nāgair acalasaṃnibhaiḥ sā yojane ca dve bhūyaḥ satyanāmā prakāśate
english: Ever full of these ever-rutting elephants, mountain-like in form, that city — true to its name — shone forth for yet another two yojanas beyond.

sanskrit: tāṃ satyanāmāṃ dṛḍhatoraṇārgalām gṛhair vicitrair upaśobhitāṃ śivām purīm ayodhyāṃ nṛsahasrasaṃkulāṃ śaśāsa vai śakrasamo mahīpatiḥ
english: That city of Ayodhyā — true to its name, with firm gates and bolts, adorned with variegated mansions, auspicious, thronged with thousands of men — was ruled by that lord of the earth equal to Śakra.
